The `fbiCDE` package wraps the FBI's Crime Data Explorer (CDE) API
(<https://cde.ucr.cjis.gov/LATEST/>), giving R users direct access to Uniform
Crime Reporting (UCR) and National Incident-Based Reporting System (NIBRS)
data: crime counts and rates, arrests, NIBRS victim/offender/offense detail,
Supplemental Homicide Reports (SHR), police employment, NIBRS participation,
and officers killed (LEOKA).

No API key is required. (`get_api_key()` and `set_api_key()` remain only for
compatibility with the package's `api.data.gov`-hosted predecessor and do
nothing.)

The CDE itself knows three geographies: the nation, a state, and a single
agency. This vignette covers those. The package also builds county, city and
metro-area views on top of them; see `vignette("geography")`.

Everything below was run against the live API on
2026-10-06. Agencies backfill and revise their
reports, so re-running it will move some numbers.


```r
library(fbiCDE)
```

## Lookups

Before requesting crime data you often need a state abbreviation, an offense
code, or an agency's ORI (the 9-character identifier the CDE uses for law
enforcement agencies).


```r
states <- get_states()
head(states)
#>   stateAbbreviation  stateName
#> 1                AL    Alabama
#> 2                AK     Alaska
#> 3                AZ    Arizona
#> 4                AR   Arkansas
#> 5                CA California
#> 6                CO   Colorado
```

`get_agency_info()` looks agencies up by name in the package's bundled agency
table (`fbi_api_agencies`), with no network call. Note that `state` here is the
full state name:


```r
get_agency_info("Oakland Police Department", state = "california", ori_only = TRUE)
#>                   agency_name       ori
#> 905 Oakland Police Department CA0010900
```

The agencies used below:

| ORI | Agency | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| `CA0010900` | Oakland Police Department, CA | crime, police employment |
| `OHCOP0000` | Columbus Police Department, OH | arrests, participation |
| `GAAPD0000` | Atlanta Police Department, GA | homicide reports |

## Summarized crime

`get_agency_crime()` returns an agency's monthly offenses and clearances;
`get_estimated_crime()` does the same for a state, or the nation when
`state_abb` is `NULL`; `get_estimated_arson()` is `get_estimated_crime()` for
arson. ("Estimated" is a legacy name: these are reported figures, not
estimates.)

The `offense` argument takes a code. The default `"V"` is violent crime and
`"P"` property crime; `get_offense_codes()` lists the rest:


```r
offenses <- get_offense_codes("crime-trend")
head(offenses, 8)
#>   code               label
#> 1  ASS  Aggravated Assault
#> 2  HOM            Homicide
#> 3  RPE                Rape
#> 4  ROB             Robbery
#> 5  ARS               Arson
#> 6  BUR            Burglary
#> 7  LAR       Larceny-theft
#> 8  MVT Motor Vehicle Theft
```


```r
oakland_crime <- get_agency_crime("CA0010900", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
oakland_crime
#>   geography offense    measure  period count   rate population
#> 1 CA0010900       V   offenses 01-2019   472 108.75     434036
#> 2 CA0010900       V   offenses 02-2019   368  84.79     434036
#> 3 CA0010900       V   offenses 03-2019   438 100.91     434036
#> 4 CA0010900       V clearances 01-2019   106  24.42     434036
#> 5 CA0010900       V clearances 02-2019    40   9.22     434036
#> 6 CA0010900       V clearances 03-2019    37   8.52     434036
#>   participated_population
#> 1                  434036
#> 2                  434036
#> 3                  434036
#> 4                  434036
#> 5                  434036
#> 6                  434036
```

Each row is one month of one `measure` (offenses or clearances). `rate` is per
100,000 people for that month. `population` is the population the agency
serves and `participated_population` the part of it covered by a report that
month; for a single agency they match whenever it reported.

For an agency or a state, the API also sends its state's and the nation's
rates for comparison. Those are dropped by default; `comparison = TRUE` keeps
them, labelled in `series` and `series_name` (they have no `count`):


```r
with_context <- get_agency_crime("CA0010900", from = "01-2019", to = "01-2019",
                                 comparison = TRUE)
with_context[, c("series", "series_name", "measure", "count", "rate")]
#>     series               series_name    measure count   rate
#> 1   agency Oakland Police Department   offenses   472 108.75
#> 2   agency Oakland Police Department clearances   106  24.42
#> 3    state                California   offenses    NA  34.38
#> 4    state                California clearances    NA  16.12
#> 5 national             United States   offenses    NA  27.85
#> 6 national             United States clearances    NA  12.20
```


```r
texas_crime <- get_estimated_crime("TX", from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
texas_crime
#>   geography offense    measure  period count  rate population
#> 1        TX       V   offenses 01-2019  9690 33.64   28995881
#> 2        TX       V   offenses 02-2019  8554 29.69   28995881
#> 3        TX       V   offenses 03-2019  9768 33.89   28995881
#> 4        TX       V clearances 01-2019  3426 11.89   28995881
#> 5        TX       V clearances 02-2019  3083 10.70   28995881
#> 6        TX       V clearances 03-2019  3266 11.33   28995881
#>   participated_population
#> 1                28804627
#> 2                28815089
#> 3                28824219
#> 4                28804627
#> 5                28815089
#> 6                28824219
```

At state and national level, `participated_population / population` is the
reporting coverage: the count is the sum of the agencies that reported, not an
estimate for everyone.


```r
national_arson <- get_estimated_arson(from = "01-2019", to = "03-2019")
national_arson[, c("geography", "measure", "period", "count", "rate")]
#>   geography    measure  period count rate
#> 1        US   offenses 01-2019  2598 0.81
#> 2        US   offenses 02-2019  2218 0.69
#> 3        US   offenses 03-2019  2771 0.86
#> 4        US clearances 01-2019   572 0.18
#> 5        US clearances 02-2019   487 0.15
#> 6        US clearances 03-2019   684 0.21
```

## Arrests

`get_arrest_count()` with the default `offense = "all"` returns monthly
arrest totals:


```r
columbus_arrests <- get_arrest_count("OHCOP0000", from = "01-2023", to = "03-2023")
columbus_arrests
#>   geography offense measure  period count  rate population
#> 1 OHCOP0000     all arrests 01-2023   617 67.89     908834
#> 2 OHCOP0000     all arrests 02-2023   606 66.68     908834
#> 3 OHCOP0000     all arrests 03-2023   674 74.16     908834
#>   participated_population
#> 1                  908834
#> 2                  908834
#> 3                  908834
```

Naming an offense returns a single total for the whole range instead: the API
has no per-offense monthly series. Names come at three levels of detail
(`list_ucr_arrest_offenses()` lists them); within one level the counts do not
overlap.


```r
head(list_ucr_arrest_offenses(level = "category"))
#> [1] "Aggravated Assault"                      
#> [2] "All Other Offenses"                      
#> [3] "Arson"                                   
#> [4] "Burglary"                                
#> [5] "Counterfeiting/Forgery"                  
#> [6] "Destruction/Damage/Vandalism of Property"

get_arrest_count(state_abb = "OH", offense = "Drug/Narcotic Offenses",
                 from = "01-2023", to = "12-2023")
#>   geography                offense measure period count rate population
#> 1        OH Drug/Narcotic Offenses arrests   <NA> 20997   NA         NA
#>   participated_population
#> 1                      NA
```

One name to watch: `"Drug Abuse Violations"` is only the drug arrests not
classed as possession or sale. The category `"Drug/Narcotic Offenses"` above
is the total.

`get_arrest_demographics()` returns arrestees by sex, race and age. The API
provides these only across *all* offenses, so `offense` must be `"all"`;
`get_arrest_demographics_all()` is a deprecated alias.


```r
oh_demographics <- get_arrest_demographics(state_abb = "OH",
                                           from = "01-2023", to = "12-2023")
head(oh_demographics)
#>   geography offense period demographic_type demographic_value  count
#> 1        OH     all   <NA>     Arrestee Sex              Male 131300
#> 2        OH     all   <NA>     Arrestee Sex            Female  56653
#> 3        OH     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race             Asian    950
#> 4        OH     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race             White 111870
#> 5        OH     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race           Unknown   7211
#> 6        OH     all   <NA>    Arrestee Race          Multiple      0
```

`vignette("juvenile-arrests")` works through these at state, agency and metro
level.

## NIBRS

`get_nibrs_victim()`, `get_nibrs_offender()` and `get_nibrs_offense()` return
one NIBRS breakdown for one offense, summed over the date range. The offense
must be a code: a summary group such as `"V"`, `"ROB"` or `"BUR"`, or a NIBRS
offense code such as `"13B"` (simple assault):


```r
head(list_nibrs_offenses(), 10)
#>    code               label
#> 1     V       Violent Crime
#> 2     P      Property Crime
#> 3   ASS  Aggravated Assault
#> 4   HOM            Homicide
#> 5   RPE                Rape
#> 6   ROB             Robbery
#> 7   ARS               Arson
#> 8   BUR            Burglary
#> 9   LAR       Larceny-theft
#> 10  MVT Motor Vehicle Theft
```


```r
get_nibrs_victim(state_abb = "OH", offense = "ROB", variable = "age",
                 from = "01-2023", to = "12-2023")
#>    geography offense period demographic_type demographic_value count
#> 1         OH     ROB                     age               0-9    29
#> 2         OH     ROB                     age             10-19   847
#> 3         OH     ROB                     age             20-29  1711
#> 4         OH     ROB                     age             30-39  1421
#> 5         OH     ROB                     age             40-49   932
#> 6         OH     ROB                     age             50-59   665
#> 7         OH     ROB                     age             60-69   455
#> 8         OH     ROB                     age             70-79   135
#> 9         OH     ROB                     age             80-89    26
#> 10        OH     ROB                     age           Unknown    25
#> 11        OH     ROB                     age          90-Older     9
```

The variables differ by function: `list_nibrs_victim_variables()`,
`list_nibrs_offender_variables()` and `list_nibrs_offense_variables()` list
them.


```r
get_nibrs_offense(state_abb = "OH", offense = "ROB", variable = "weapons",
                  from = "01-2023", to = "12-2023")[, c("demographic_value", "count")]
#>                 demographic_value count
#> 1                            None  2615
#> 2                           Other   116
#> 3                           Rifle    24
#> 4                          Poison     1
#> 5                         Firearm   474
#> 6                         Handgun  1332
#> 7                         Shotgun     9
#> 8                         Unknown   221
#> 9                      Explosives     2
#> 10                   Asphyxiation     3
#> 11                   Blunt Object    68
#> 12                  Other Firearm    24
#> 13               Personal Weapons   928
#> 14              Rifle (Automatic)     1
#> 15            Firearm (Automatic)     0
#> 16            Handgun (Automatic)    31
#> 17            Shotgun (Automatic)     0
#> 18           Motor Vehicle/Vessel    28
#> 19         Fire/Incendiary Device     2
#> 20       Knife/Cutting Instrument   239
#> 21      Other Firearm (Automatic)     0
#> 22 Drugs/Narcotics/Sleeping Pills     2
```

An offense *name* returns no data from the API, so the package rejects it and
suggests the code:


```r
get_nibrs_victim(state_abb = "OH", offense = "robbery")
#> Error: 'robbery' is not a NIBRS offense code; the API returns no data for offense names. Did you mean "ROB" (Robbery)? See list_nibrs_offenses().
```

An agency or state that did not report to NIBRS in the period returns no rows,
with a message.

## Supplemental Homicide Reports (SHR)

`get_shr()` returns monthly homicide counts from the SHR, for an agency, a
state, or the nation:


```r
get_shr(ori = "GAAPD0000", from = "01-2019", to = "06-2019")
#>   geography  period count
#> 1 GAAPD0000 01-2019     8
#> 2 GAAPD0000 02-2019     9
#> 3 GAAPD0000 03-2019     9
#> 4 GAAPD0000 04-2019     7
#> 5 GAAPD0000 05-2019     7
#> 6 GAAPD0000 06-2019     7
```

A zero can mean "not reported". Florida, for one, sends almost no SHR data:


```r
fl <- get_shr(state_abb = "FL", from = "01-2019", to = "12-2019")
ga <- get_shr(state_abb = "GA", from = "01-2019", to = "12-2019")
c(Florida = sum(fl$count), Georgia = sum(ga$count))
#> Florida Georgia 
#>       9     484
```

## Police employment

`get_police_employment()` uses four-digit years rather than `MM-YYYY`:


```r
oakland_pe <- get_police_employment("CA0010900", from = "2018", to = "2020")
oakland_pe
#>   year male_officers female_officers male_civilians female_civilians       ori
#> 1 2018           633              98             60              219 CA0010900
#> 2 2019           636             104             63              220 CA0010900
#> 3 2020           632             108             83              233 CA0010900
#>   male_total female_total civilians_total officers_total employees_total
#> 1        693          317             279            731            1010
#> 2        699          324             283            740            1023
#> 3        715          341             316            740            1056
```

Staffing is published for individual agencies only. The API accepts a state,
a region or the nation, but answers with every value missing -- counts and
rates alike -- so `get_police_employment()` returns no rows and says why:


```r
nrow(get_police_employment(state_abb = "TX", from = "2018", to = "2020"))
#> get_police_employment() returned no data for TX, 2018-2020. The CDE currently publishes police staffing for individual agencies only; state, region and national requests come back empty.
#> [1] 0
```

## NIBRS participation

`get_agency_participation()`, `get_state_participation()` and
`get_region_participation()` report whether agencies report to NIBRS *now*,
from the live agency directory. They are a current snapshot, not a history,
and they count agencies, not people: a state with few NIBRS agencies can still
have near-complete reporting coverage through the older summary system (see
the `participated_population` columns above).


```r
get_agency_participation("OHCOP0000")
#>         ori                agency_name agency_type_name state_abbr state_name
#> 1 OHCOP0000 Columbus Police Department             City         OH       Ohio
#>                          county is_nibrs nibrs_start_date
#> 1 DELAWARE, FAIRFIELD, FRANKLIN     TRUE       2003-01-01
```


```r
get_state_participation("OH")
#>   state_abbr total_agencies nibrs_agencies participation_rate
#> 1         OH            863            831            0.96292
```


```r
get_region_participation("South")
#>   region total_agencies nibrs_agencies participation_rate
#> 1  South           8119           7105          0.8751078
```

## Officers killed (LEOKA)

`get_leoka()` and `get_leoka_monthly()` return national counts of law
enforcement officers **feloniously killed**, from 2020 on. Despite the
program's name (Law Enforcement Officers Killed and Assaulted) these are not
assault counts. The API returns national figures only.


```r
get_leoka(2020, 2021)
#>   year month total_officers total_incidents total_officers_dod
#> 1 2020    NA             46              44                  2
#> 2 2021    NA             73              68                  4
#>   total_officers_doi total_incidents_dod total_incidents_doi
#> 1                 44                   2                  42
#> 2                 69                   4                  64
```


```r
get_leoka_monthly(2021, 1)
#>   year month total_officers total_incidents total_officers_dod
#> 1 2021     1              6               4                  0
#>   total_officers_doi total_incidents_dod total_incidents_doi
#> 1                  6                   0                   4
```
